featured_reviews.name: Kishor Pansare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this restaurant on the way to Crawford Market. I’ve been coming here since childhood—not very regularly, but occasionally.I went for kheema pav, but the owner suggested bheja along with kheema pav, so I went with his recommendation.

When the dish arrived, the portion size was quite small and didn’t feel worth ₹240. On top of that, they charge ₹20 extra for pav, which feels a bit excessive. The taste was very good—rich and flavorful—but slightly too spicy and oily for my liking.

In the afternoon, the place is usually packed, especially for non-vegetarian dishes. However, as a local Mumbaikar, I do feel the pricing is on the higher side. Either the cost should be more reasonable or the portion size should be increased to justify it.

The owner was actively moving around, asking customers for feedback and promoting items like fish fry, caramel custard, and solkadhi. While this does help in building customer relationships, a major drawback comes at the time of billing—they do not accept UPI payments, only cash.

featured_reviews.name: Curious Fork
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Feast Worth the Journey from Pune!
We travelled all the way from Pune just to eat at Hotel Grant House, and it was worth every minute. This restaurant has been on our bucket list for a while, and it thoroughly satisfied our hunger. We left full and sent them a lot of blessings for such delicious food!  We were hungry so didn't have the patience to take pictures to post.
The Fried Bombil, Crab Lollipop, Prawns Masala, and Prawns Pulav were outstanding. The river prawns were sweet and cooked perfectly.Mutton Khima was flavourful, well-spiced, and delicious. Their last portion of caramel custard had our name on it, so glad! That was so good too.
The staff is incredibly polite and attentive. A special thanks to the manager, Shridhar, who suggested a few items every single recommendation was spot on and scrumptious.
The restaurant is located in a crowded area and the street is not well lit but the food is so good that the surroundings do not matter. It is a definitive must-try place if you are in the area. We only wish they had a branch in Pune!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Just experienced a fantastic meal at the iconic Bharat Excellensea, a 35-year-old gem in Mumbai's Ballard Estate! The restaurant has been recently revamped, and the ambiance is now even more inviting. But the real star is the food!

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

Visited Mahesh Lunch Home and had a wonderful dining experience. We tried the Butter Garlic Prawns, Crab Lollipop, Jumbo Tawa Prawns, and Chicken Biryani. The seafood was fresh, perfectly cooked, and packed with flavor. The Butter Garlic Prawns were rich and delicious, while the Jumbo Tawa Prawns stood out with their excellent seasoning. The Crab Lollipop was crispy and enjoyable, and the Chicken Biryani was aromatic and satisfying.

A special mention for their Solkadi, which is always on the darker side. While it has a distinctive flavor, I feel a slightly lighter preparation could bring more subtlety and balance, making it even more refreshing and enjoyable to sip alongside the seafood.

The service was attentive, and the overall ambiance made for a great meal. Definitely a place worth visiting for seafood lovers. Highly recommended!

The Chicken Chettinad was amazing—rich, aromatic, and authentic, with a well-rounded masala that really stood out. The squid was also quite tasty, fresh, and cooked just right.

The place itself has a nice ambience, is clean and hygienic, and the overall quality of food is clearly well maintained. The staff are very friendly, polite, and attentive, which adds positively to the experience.

While the prices are on the higher side, the quality, hygiene, and taste justify the cost. A good place for quality food and a relaxed dining experience—definitely worth a visit. Only issue is Parking. Better to go in a taxi.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahesh Lunch Lounge was an absolute standout and easily one of our best meals in India. We chose to eat here over the Taj after it was strongly recommended by locals — and we are so glad we listened. From start to finish, the experience was fantastic.

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

Follow ➡️ @daddylittlelunchbox

featured_reviews.review_text:
Pratap Lunch Home is a great spot if you’re craving prawns or fish. I tried their butter garlic prawns (4/5), tawa surmai fry (4/5), and Chettinad prawn biryani (4/5). It’s a chill place with a coastal vibe and homely food—highly recommend for a quick lunch.
Top Dishes
•	Butter garlic prawns: Fresh and flavorful, hitting all the right garlicky notes without overpowering the seafood.
•	Tawa surmai fry: Crispy edges with balanced spices, showcasing the fish’s natural freshness.
•	Chettinad prawn biryani: Spicy, aromatic, and generously portioned for a satisfying coastal twist.
Vibe and Service
The relaxed, sea-inspired ambience pairs perfectly with the comforting, home-style cooking. Quick service makes it ideal for lunch breaks in the Fort area.

featured_reviews.name: Niki Mitra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Discover the flavors of the sea at Pratap Lunch Home, a hidden restaurant de fruits de mer in the heart of Fort, Mumbai! This seafood and non-veg lover's paradise is a must-visit for any food enthusiast.

The LOVE:

- Delicious Food: The dishes are packed with flavor, and the portions are generous.
- Friendly Staff: The team is attentive and welcoming, making sure you feel at home.
- Cozy Ambiance: The AC section is a blessing, especially during peak hours.
- Alcohol Served: With a 10% VAT, you can pair your meal with a drink of your choice.

Must-Try Dishes:

- Mutton Bhuna: Tender, spicy, and utterly addictive. The quantity is impressive, and the quality shines through.
- Prawns Chilly Roast: Fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. A must-try for seafood lovers.

We were impressed by the food, service, and ambiance. While peak hours can get busy, the wait is worth it. We're already planning our next visit to try more of their menu offerings.

If you're a seafood or non-veg lover, Pratap Lunch Home is a must-visit destination. With its rich flavors and cozy atmosphere, it's a great spot for a night out with friends or a special occasion.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great culinary experience having lunch here on a weekday with my family. The place was not crowded at all, the ambience was calm and inviting with a home-like touch. We came with the intention of enjoying seafood and we achieved exactly that. I definitely recommend dining here and Pratap Lunch Home is now on my must-return list!

Food we ordered:
Bombil Fry - A Bombay staple and they did it justice. (5/5)
Lobster Chilly Roast - This was my favourite. Unbelievably good! I also liked how they were transparent in showing us the sizes and prices of the lobster they had in their catch and let us choose as per our preference. (5/5)
King Prawns Ghee Roast - Also really good. (5/5)
Shell Fish Sukka - Good masala but we were not blown away. We also had to be extra careful while eating as not all hard debris were cleaned from the shell fish. (3/5)
Squid Malabar - Crispy fried squid which I couldn't get enough of. (5/5)
Prawns Vijaywada - Decently flavoured prawns curry. (4/5)
Mutton Tawa Pulao - I've never had pulao done so well. Good sized portion too. (5/5)

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text: This unassuming spot might just serve some of the best fried prawns in the city. The tiny interiors and no-frills ambiance could easily mislead a first-time visitor, but the food quickly sets the record straight. The prawns are succulent and perfectly cooked, encased in a crisp, red coloured batter that achieves just the right balance of texture and flavour. The accompanying green chutney is a standout, adding a zesty punch that elevates the dish to another level. At Rs. 234 for a modest 150g portion, it’s not exactly a budget option, but the quality makes it a fair deal. These prawns would pair beautifully with a chilled beverage of your choice if you’re planning a casual meal at home. That said, there’s a certain charm in enjoying them right there, standing on the street. The service is quick, making it a convenient stop before catching a movie at the nearby Metro Theatre. Whether you’re in the mood for fried fish, chicken, prawns, or Pomfret, this spot delivers a consistently satisfying, indulgent experience—a classic that’s earned its reputation in the area.

featured_reviews.review_text: We visited The Bayview Restaurant @ Marine Plaza to celebrate our daughter's birthday. It was amazing to sit by the window and watch Marine Drive hustle-bustle. We had seen a particular delicacy in their online menu and we inquired whether it was available since we couldn't see it in the menu. Sakshi assured that she would request the chef to make the dish since the new menu had  come into recently. When she realised that we were there to celebrate our daughter's birthday, she arranged for a cake on the house with an announcement by the live music band. It made the birthday girl feel special and amazing. We had a fab time. Thanks for making the evening so special.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Talwalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A 70-year-old iconic establishment of South Bombay, it has long been at the center of fine dining for stars and socialites alike. It was frequently patronized by the likes of Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, and many cricketers. Recently renovated, you step into a regal experience - complete with uniformed waitstaff, European Art Deco accents, and live music.

The menu offers a unique mix of Indian dishes, a few European selections, and non-alcoholic beverages. Unique, because an ambience like this almost demands a glass of wine - something you sorely miss as piano renditions of old and new Bollywood compositions play on.

The food is excellent, the service could be better, but the experience is a must-have. One that transports you back to the charm of old Bombay.

featured_reviews.name: Anannya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a place that blends old-school charm with a premium, aesthetic vibe, this is the one. I visited this iconic spot near Marine Lines and honestly, the ambience itself sets the mood. Loved the seating and the service.

What we tried:
Summer Breeze 4.5⭐
Quattro Formaggi  5⭐

The pasta was the highlight as it was runny, rich and sauce. The portion size would be easily filling for two. The mocktail could’ve been sweeter, but still enjoyable.

Make a reservation if you’re planning to go on weekends or during peak dinner hours, it gets busy. Overall, I would rate a 5/5. Definitely going back to explore more on the menu.

featured_reviews.name: Mahesh Maurya
featured_reviews.review_text:

On the positive side, the environment and ambiance of the restaurant were quite good—clean, comfortable, and pleasant for dining with friends or family. The staff was polite, and considering the location, the prices are affordable and value for money.

If the restaurant could focus on improving the quality of service, especially ensuring that the food is served hot, it would definitely enhance the overall dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text: We set out on a magnificent culinary adventure at the newly launched Pali Bhavan at Eros, a true gastronomic treasure that shines bright with its sublime Indian cuisine. The ambiance was very laid back, bathed in a warm glow by colonial decor and softly radiant lights. Our delightful odyssey commenced with Tandoori pomfret, Galouti kebab, Malai chicken tikka, and prawn, each dish a brilliant testament to the chef's innovative genius. The main course showcased their legendary crab Sukkha and Kali Dal, masterfully crafted to exhilarate the senses. The crowning glory was the paan kulfi and chocolate roshogolla, desserts that left us utterly enchanted. The food was truly sublime, with flavors that joyfully danced on the palate and desserts that stole the spotlight, rendering the entire experience profoundly unforgettable.

featured_reviews.name: Aakash
featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s an unmistakable old-world charm here; an almost nostalgic, lived-in elegance that feels refreshingly authentic in a city that often chases the new and shiny.

The ambience is wonderfully understated: warm lighting, vintage touches, wooden furniture that has seen stories, and that classic Bombay colonial-meets-Bandra vibe.

The food is rich, deeply flavoured, cooked with real care. Every dish carries that unmistakable depth; nothing is timid or overly polished. The spicing is confident, the portions generous, and the execution consistent. It’s the kind of meal that lingers in memory long after you’ve left.

Whether it’s a quiet celebration, a catch-up with old friends, or simply craving something soulful, Pali Bhavan delivers exactly what one hopes for in a neighbourhood favourite: character, flavour, and comfort in equal measure.

Highly recommended for those who appreciate substance over spectacle.

featured_reviews.name: Paul
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a lovely restaurant with absolutely amazing food. Every dish we had was fantastic - some of the best food we have had whilst in India. Friendly and attentive staff and the restaurant has a lovely atmosphere. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Monis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Pali Bhavan is less like walking into a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a world carefully curated for the senses. The moment you cross the threshold, a warm, vibrant energy wraps around you — the kind that hums with quiet excitement and makes you instantly glad you came. The interiors are a masterclass in rustic vintage design: weathered textures, artful nostalgia, and thoughtful details that together create an atmosphere that feels both timeless and distinctly alive.

The food is, simply put, exceptional. Every dish arrives as evidence of a kitchen that takes its craft seriously — where quality is not a checkbox but a standard. The menu reads like a love letter to bold, imaginative cooking: innovative, eye-catching, and refreshingly unhurried in its approach. Dish after dish finds a way to surprise, with flavours that linger long after the last bite and an unmistakable ability to awaken the palate in ways you didn't expect.

Equally deserving of praise is the service. The staff carries a warmth that feels genuine — attentive without being intrusive, welcoming without being performative. They move through the room with ease, and their care for the guest experience is palpable. Dining here never once feels rushed; instead, it unfolds at exactly the right pace for a truly relaxed, enjoyable evening.

"Pali Bhavan doesn't just offer a meal — it offers an experience worthy of returning to. South Mumbai has quietly welcomed a new icon, and those who discover it will find themselves planning their next visit before the first one is even over."

featured_reviews.name: Govind Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pizza By The Bay is truly one of Mumbai’s most iconic dining destinations, offering the perfect combination of great food, vibrant ambience, and an unbeatable sea-facing location on Marine Drive. The moment you step in, you’re welcomed by a lively, energetic vibe that instantly sets the mood for a memorable dining experience.
The biggest highlight is, without a doubt, the stunning view of the Arabian Sea. If you’re lucky enough to get a window-side seat, the experience becomes even more special—watching the waves while enjoying your meal is pure Mumbai magic. Whether it’s breakfast with the morning breeze, an evening meal with city lights, or a monsoon visit with rain and waves in the backdrop, the atmosphere here is always captivating.
The food quality is consistently good and flavorful. Their pizzas are perfectly baked with rich toppings and bold flavors, making them one of the best pizza spots in the city. Pasta, garlic bread, sandwiches, and breakfast options are equally satisfying. Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes are well prepared, and the menu offers enough variety to suit different tastes, though a few items may feel premium-priced for the portions. Desserts and beverages like hot chocolate also stand out.
The ambience deserves special mention—antique-style décor, warm lighting, and a classy yet relaxed crowd give the place a timeless charm. It’s suitable for everything from solo visits and casual meet-ups to professional meetings and weekend outings. The place does get quite crowded, especially during peak hours and weekends, and waiting times can be long, but the experience is worth the patience.
Service is efficient and friendly, with staff guiding you well through the menu and attending promptly despite the crowd. While the lively atmosphere can make it a bit noisy, it adds to the overall energy of the place rather than taking away from it.
Overall, Pizza By The Bay is a must-visit for anyone who loves good food paired with a spectacular sea view. Slightly on the expensive side and often crowded, but the location, vibe, and quality make it a memorable 5-star experience. Perfect for creating beautiful Mumbai memories.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Umm..nice Thali experience. We didn't have to wait for a table coz we got there early.
Space is very cramped though. Only 4 tables in the AC section, that too, 2 of them sharing a boundary with the washroom...ewww..not good for a dine out.
The thali is very basic. Rice, curry, bhakri/chapatis, sliced onion, whatever fried fish you order & dried prawns. 🍤🐟That's it. No solkadi, no desert, no salad. Nothing.
For the price, not VFM.

Only 1 boy to take orders from all tables + handle the Zomato/ Swiggy orders. He was rushed.
Yet, he was polite and courteous. Good going.

The gravy is extremely spicy 🔥🥵. Not for the faint-hearted. Had to forego half of it.
The fish is fresh, though.

Several patrons who asked for BOMBIL, were turned down bcz it wasn't available. Not great, since a seafood place ought to have these by default (one of the crowd favourites). Or ..perhaps ...being a Sunday, Tarri was trying to push the other costlier fish..who knows?? 🤔Anyways, the portion of fried prawns was decent.
No soft drinks available besides the bottled fizzies. The soft drinks were all warm & not chilled or cool post 12 noon. 🥤
And solkadi, which was just made, was not cooled before serving, post 1 p.m.
No desserts, except kharvas (decent) & caramel custard.🍮
Return if you want to sample other dishes, if not, would not recommend a second visit.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)
